evidence_quotes.quote: there is no legal water connection, water is supplied

publication_year_note: Primary journal volume/issue year is 2023 (GeoJournal (2023) 88:3183-3204); published online 1 December 2022 (copyright 2022).
rationale: Full text read (22 pages). Although the paper substantively compares two Dhaka slums with legalized DWASA water connections (Korail and Baganbari) against one frequently evicted slum relying on informal/illegal private vendors (Tejgaon) using a stratified household survey (N = 150, 50 per slum) alongside FGDs, IDIs and KIIs, all empirical comparisons of water prices, water expenditure shares, per-capita consumption (lpcd), open defecation rates (Table 3, p. 11), pair-wise problem rankings (Table 4, p. 11) and PCA-weighted composite Water Security Index scores (WSI = 6.2, 2.8 and 3.4; Fig. 3, p. 14) are strictly descriptive without any inferential statistical tests, regression estimates, standard errors, confidence intervals, t-statistics, chi-square statistics or p-values (the only other quantitative metrics are goodness-of-fit bias-correction statistics PBIAS, NSE, MAE and RMSE for regional climate temperature downscaling in Table 5, p. 16). Flagging this study as eligible for inferential quantitative synthesis is therefore overstated.
